s: Put the raspberries, coconut milk, almond milk, erythritol and vanilla in the blender.
Blend for 1 minute until smooth.
Add the chia seeds and blend for just 5 seconds.
Let stand for 5 minutes so the chia thickens slightly, then serve.
l10-smoothie-framboise-coco.p: With frozen raspberries, the smoothie turns into an almost drinkable ice cream.

l10-the-vert-gingembre-citron.t: Green tea infusion with ginger and lemon
i: water for the green tea (2 tea bags)
s: Simmer the water with the ginger slices for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let cool for 2 minutes: green tea should not steep in boiling water.
Add the green tea and steep for 3 minutes, then remove it.
Add the lemon juice, sweeten with stevia and serve hot or iced.
l10-the-vert-gingembre-citron.p: After 3 minutes, green tea turns bitter. Delicious iced in summer.

s: Put the almond milk, cream, vanilla and erythritol in the blender.
Add the whey on top so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Add the ice cubes and blend for 45 seconds until thick and frothy.
Serve immediately in tall glasses.
l10-milkshake-vanille-proteine.p: Ideal after a workout. Add 1 tbsp of peanut butter for a more indulgent version.

s: Wash and hull the strawberries.
Put all the ingredients in the blender.
Blend for 1 minute until very smooth and frothy.
Serve chilled with a few ice cubes.
l10-smoothie-fraise-amande.p: Freeze seasonal strawberries in summer to enjoy them all year round.

l11-moelleux-chocolat.t: Dark chocolate and almond fudgy cake
s: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Grease a 22 cm round pan and line the bottom with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bain-marie over low heat, stirring, then let cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the eggs with the erythritol, vanilla and salt for 3 minutes until pale and doubled in volume.
Pour the melted chocolate over the eggs, folding gently with a spatula.
Fold in the sifted almond flour, lifting the batter without overworking it.
Pour into the pan and bake for 20 to 22 minutes: the center should still be slightly wobbly.
Let cool for 15 minutes before unmolding; serve warm or cold.
l11-moelleux-chocolat.p: Keeps for 4 days in the refrigerator; microwave a slice for 15 seconds to bring back the molten center.

s: Preheat the oven to 210°C. Grease 4 ramekins and dust them with cocoa, tapping out the excess.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a bain-marie, stir until smooth and let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, yolk and erythritol for 2 minutes, then add the melted chocolate.
Fold in the almond flour and fill the ramekins three-quarters full.
Bake for exactly 8 to 9 minutes: the edges are set, the center domed and soft.
Wait 1 minute, run a knife around the edges and turn out onto a plate. Serve immediately.
l11-fondant-coeur-coulant.p: Prepare the ramekins up to 24 hours ahead and keep them in the refrigerator; add 2 minutes to the baking time.

l11-cake-citron.t: Moist lemon loaf cake with light glaze
s: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a loaf pan with baking paper.
Whisk the eggs with 80 g of erythritol, then add the melted butter, yogurt, zest and 40 ml of lemon juice.
In a separate bowl, mix the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder and salt, then fold into the wet ingredients.
Pour into the pan and bake for 40 minutes; cover with foil halfway through if the top browns too much.
Check doneness with a knife blade: it should come out dry. Let cool completely on a rack.
Blitz the remaining 20 g of erythritol into a powder, mix with the rest of the lemon juice and drizzle over the cooled cake.
l11-cake-citron.p: The cake is even better the next day; it freezes well in individually wrapped slices.

l11-carrot-cake-leger.t: Light carrot cake with walnuts and cinnamon
i: cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg
s: Preheat the oven to 175°C and grease a 20 cm square pan.
Finely grate the carrot and squeeze it in a tea towel to remove excess water.
Whisk the eggs with the erythritol and coconut oil, then add the carrot.
Fold in the almond flour, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and walnuts.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a knife comes out dry. Let cool.
Whisk the cream cheese with the vanilla and stevia, then spread over the cooled cake before cutting into 10 squares.
l11-carrot-cake-leger.p: Keep the frosting separate if you make the cake ahead; it keeps for 4 days in the refrigerator.

s: Preheat the oven to 180°C and oil a 22 cm pan.
Whisk the eggs with the erythritol until frothy.
Add the coconut milk, melted coconut oil and vanilla.
Fold in the shredded coconut, almond flour and baking powder; let stand for 5 minutes so the coconut hydrates.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 minutes until the top is nicely golden.
Let cool in the pan before unmolding and cutting into 8 slices.
l11-gateau-coco.p: Sprinkle with shredded coconut toasted dry in a skillet for 2 minutes for a crunchy finish.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Mix the almond flour, melted butter and 20 g of erythritol, and press into the bottom of a 22 cm springform pan.
Pre-bake the base for 10 minutes, then let cool. Lower the oven to 150°C.
Beat the cream cheese (at room temperature) with 90 g of erythritol on low speed until smooth.
Add the sour cream, vanilla and lemon, then the eggs one at a time, without beating too fast so you don't incorporate air.
Pour over the base, place a dish of hot water on the bottom rack and bake for 50 minutes: the center should still wobble.
Turn off the oven and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour with the door slightly open, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours before unmolding.
l11-cheesecake-new-york.p: Serve with a raspberry coulis heated for 5 minutes with a pinch of stevia.

s: Blend the almonds with the melted butter and 10 g of erythritol, press into the bottom of a 20 cm ring set on a plate and chill.
Blend 100 g of raspberries with the lemon. Dissolve the agar-agar in the water, bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes, stirring.
Off the heat, add the raspberry purée to the hot agar-agar and stir briskly.
Smooth the cream cheese with 60 g of erythritol, then quickly fold in the still-warm raspberry mixture.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and gently fold it in with a spatula.
Pour over the base, decorate with the remaining raspberries and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before removing the ring.
l11-cheesecake-framboise-sans-cuisson.p: Work quickly after adding the agar-agar: it sets as soon as it drops below 40°C.

s: Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie and let it cool to about 35°C.
Separate the whites from the yolks. Stir the yolks into the chocolate one at a time, mixing briskly.
Whip the whites with the salt to soft peaks, add the erythritol and whisk until firm and glossy.
Mix a third of the whites into the chocolate to loosen it, then gently fold in the rest, lifting with a spatula.
Divide among 6 small glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
l11-mousse-chocolat.p: Use very fresh eggs and eat within 48 hours. Serve with a few raspberries. Contains raw eggs: not recommended for pregnant women, children under 5, or elderly or vulnerable people.

s: Chill the can of coconut cream in the refrigerator for 12 hours, and put the bowl and whisks in the freezer for 15 minutes.
Scoop out only the solid part of the coconut cream and whisk for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Add the erythritol, vanilla, zest, then the lemon juice little by little, whisking continuously.
Divide among 4 dessert cups, sprinkle with toasted coconut and refrigerate for 1 hour.
l11-mousse-citron-coco.p: Keep the leftover coconut liquid for a smoothie or a curry.

s: Preheat the oven to 150°C and place 6 ramekins in a large baking dish.
Heat the cream and almond milk until simmering, then remove from the heat.
Whisk the yolks with the erythritol and vanilla without making them foamy, then pour in the hot liquid in a thin stream, stirring.
Strain, divide among the ramekins and pour hot water into the dish to halfway up the ramekins.
Bake for 35 minutes: the custard should be set at the edges and slightly wobbly in the center.
Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours.
l11-creme-vanille.p: Save the egg whites for coconut macaroons or a chocolate mousse.

s: Preheat the oven to 100°C.
Heat the cream until simmering, remove from the heat and add the vanilla and orange blossom water.
Whisk the yolks with 40 g of erythritol, then slowly pour in the hot cream, stirring.
Divide among 4 shallow crème brûlée dishes and bake for 45 minutes, until the custard is set.
Let cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle with the remaining 20 g of erythritol and caramelize with a kitchen torch or for 2 minutes under a very hot broiler.
l11-creme-brulee-fleur-oranger.p: Erythritol caramelizes less than sugar: spread it in a very thin layer and watch it under the broiler.

s: Whisk the coconut milk with the agar-agar and 30 g of erythritol in a cold saucepan.
Bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Divide among 4 glasses and let set for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Crush the raspberries with the lemon and 10 g of erythritol, then spoon over the panna cottas before serving.
l11-panna-cotta-coco-framboise.p: Fully plant-based, ideal for lactose-intolerant children.

s: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a baking sheet with baking paper.
Cream the softened butter with the erythritol, then add the egg and vanilla.
Fold in the almond flour, baking powder and salt, then the chocolate pieces.
Refrigerate the dough for 15 minutes so it holds its shape.
Shape 12 balls and flatten them slightly, spacing them 5 cm apart on the sheet.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the edges turn golden; let firm up for 10 minutes on the sheet before moving.
l11-cookies-pepites-chocolat.p: The cookies are soft when they come out of the oven: they firm up as they cool. Airtight container: 5 days.

s: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a baking sheet with baking paper.
Mix the peanut butter, erythritol, egg and salt until you have a smooth dough.
Shape 12 balls, place them on the sheet and flatten them with a fork in a crisscross pattern.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, then let cool completely on the sheet before handling.
l11-cookies-beurre-cacahuete.p: Add a pinch of flaky sea salt to each cookie before baking for a sweet-salty contrast.

s: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a 20 cm square pan with baking paper.
Melt the chocolate and butter together, then let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs and erythritol for 2 minutes, then add the melted chocolate.
Fold in the almond flour, cocoa and salt, then the chopped walnuts.
Spread in the pan and bake for 20 to 22 minutes: a knife should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Let cool completely, ideally 1 hour in the refrigerator, before cutting into 12 squares.
l11-brownie-noix.p: The brownie slices cleanly after a stint in the refrigerator; it freezes very well.

s: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a 20 cm pan.
Melt the chocolate with the butter and let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs with the erythritol, add the chocolate, then the almond flour and cocoa.
Pour into the pan. Loosen the tahini with 1 tbsp of hot water and drop it in spoonfuls over the batter.
Swirl with the tip of a knife in figure eights, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 20 minutes, let cool and cut into 12 squares.
l11-brownie-tahini.p: Stir the tahini jar well before use; the oil often rises to the surface.

s: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Mix the fruit with 20 g of erythritol and the cinnamon, then spread in a baking dish.
Rub together the almond flour, 30 g of erythritol and the cold butter with your fingertips until you have large crumbs.
Add the flaked almonds and spread the crumble over the fruit without packing it down.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.
l11-crumble-fruits-rouges-amande.p: Serve with a spoonful of Greek yogurt or thick sour cream.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Mix the almond flour, 50 g of melted butter, 20 g of erythritol and the salt.
Press the dough into a 22 cm tart pan, pushing it up the sides, prick with a fork and blind-bake for 12 minutes.
In a saucepan, whisk the eggs, 80 g of erythritol, the zest and the lemon juice.
Thicken over low heat, whisking constantly, for 5 to 7 minutes, until it reaches the consistency of thick cream; do not let it boil.
Off the heat, add 60 g of diced butter and blend for 1 minute to smooth it out.
Pour over the cooled tart shell and refrigerate for 3 hours before serving.
l11-tarte-citron-sablee.p: The tart shell is fragile: let it cool completely in the pan before filling.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Mix 130 g of almond flour, 40 g of melted butter, 15 g of erythritol and the salt, then press into a 22 cm pan.
Pre-bake the base for 10 minutes.
For the almond cream, whisk 60 g of softened butter with 65 g of erythritol, then add the eggs, vanilla and 100 g of almond flour.
Spread the almond cream over the base and bake for 20 minutes until golden and firm.
Let cool completely, then arrange the halved strawberries on top just before serving.
l11-tarte-amandine-fraises.p: Replace the strawberries with raspberries or blackberries depending on the season.

s: Take the strawberries out of the freezer 5 minutes ahead so they soften slightly.
Pulse them in a powerful blender with the erythritol and lemon.
Pour in the cream in a thin stream, blending until you get a soft-serve texture.
Serve immediately, or freeze for 30 minutes for a firmer texture.
l11-glace-fraise.p: If kept in the freezer for more than 2 hours, take it out 15 minutes before serving, as erythritol makes it freeze hard.

s: Heat the water and erythritol for 3 minutes until completely dissolved, then let cool.
Blend the raspberries with the syrup and lemon, then strain through a fine sieve to remove the seeds.
Pour into a container and freeze; every 30 minutes for 3 hours, scrape and stir vigorously with a fork.
Just before serving, quickly blend the crystals for a smooth texture.
l11-sorbet-framboise.p: With an ice cream maker, churn for 25 minutes after chilling the mixture for 2 hours in the refrigerator.

s: Whisk the yolks with the erythritol. Heat the almond milk and 100 ml of cream until simmering.
Pour the hot liquid over the yolks, return to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring, until the custard coats the spoon (82°C), without boiling.
Add the vanilla, strain and let cool completely in the refrigerator.
Whip the remaining 300 ml of cream to soft peaks and fold it into the cold custard.
Pour into a container and freeze for 6 hours, stirring with a fork after 1 hour and again after 2 hours.
l11-glace-vanille-sans-sorbetiere.p: Take the ice cream out 10 to 15 minutes before serving so it is easy to scoop.

s: Finely chop the chocolate and place it in a bowl.
Bring the cream and erythritol to a simmer and pour over the chocolate. Wait 1 minute, then stir from the center outward.
Add the butter, smooth the ganache and refrigerate for 2 hours until firm.
Scoop portions with a teaspoon and quickly roll between your palms into 20 balls.
Roll them in the cocoa and keep refrigerated.
l11-truffes-chocolat-cacao.p: Vary the coating: shredded coconut, pistachios or chopped hazelnuts. Two truffles per serving.

s: Melt 60 g of coconut oil over very low heat, then mix with the shredded coconut, erythritol and vanilla.
Divide among 12 silicone mini muffin molds and press down with the back of a spoon.
Freeze for 20 minutes to harden.
Melt the chocolate with the remaining 20 g of coconut oil and coat each bite.
Return to the cold for 15 minutes and store in the refrigerator.
l11-fat-bombs-coco-chocolat.p: One or two bites are enough to calm a sweet craving; they keep for 2 weeks in the refrigerator.

l11-fat-bombs-cacahuete.t: Frozen peanut butter and chocolate bites
s: Whisk the peanut butter, cream cheese, softened butter and erythritol until you have a smooth cream.
Divide among 12 paper liners set in a muffin pan.
Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie and drizzle over each bite.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts and freeze for 1 hour before unmolding.
Store in the freezer and take out 5 minutes before eating.
l11-fat-bombs-cacahuete.p: Keep them in a box in the freezer: they are enjoyed like little melting ice cubes.

s: Melt the butter in a mug for 15 seconds in the microwave.
Add the egg, erythritol and vanilla, and whisk with a fork.
Fold in the almond flour and baking powder, then push the raspberries into the batter.
Microwave for 80 seconds at 800 W and let stand for 1 minute before eating.
l11-mug-cake-vanille-framboise.p: Replace the raspberries with blueberries or blackberries, or add some lemon zest.

s: Whisk the eggs with 70 g of erythritol and the vanilla until foamy.
Add the coconut oil, shredded coconut, almond flour and baking powder; let rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Blitz the remaining 20 g of erythritol into a fine powder.
Shape 24 balls, roll them in the powdered erythritol and place on a lined baking sheet.
Bake for 15 minutes until the ghribas are cracked and barely golden at the base.
l11-ghriba-coco.p: Keep for a week in a tin box, perfect with sugar-free mint tea.

s: Filling: finely grind the blanched almonds with the erythritol, add 20 g of butter, the cinnamon and 3 tsp of orange blossom water, and knead into a pliable paste.
Shape 24 small logs of filling, tapered at the ends, and set aside.
Dough: mix the almond flour and psyllium, add the egg, 40 g of melted butter and 1 tsp of orange blossom water; knead and let rest for 15 minutes.
Roll the dough very thin (2 mm) between two sheets of baking paper and cut strips 8 cm wide.
Place a log of filling on a strip, fold the dough over, seal by pressing, cut with a pastry wheel and curve into a crescent.
Prick each horn with a needle and bake for 12 to 15 minutes at 170°C: they should stay pale.
Let cool completely before handling; the dough is fragile when warm.
l11-cornes-gazelle.p: If the dough cracks, work it between two sheets and mend it with a damp fingertip. Two horns per serving.

l11-fekkas-amandes.t: Keto fekkas with almonds and anise
s: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Whisk the eggs with the erythritol, melted butter and orange blossom water.
Add the almond flour, baking powder, anise, sesame and whole almonds; mix into a sticky dough.
With wet hands, shape two logs 4 cm in diameter on a lined baking sheet.
Bake for 20 minutes until the logs are firm and light golden. Let cool for 30 minutes.
Slice the logs with a serrated knife into 1 cm biscuits and lay them flat.
Lower the oven to 140°C and dry them for 20 minutes, turning halfway through, until crisp.
l11-fekkas-amandes.p: Once completely cooled, they keep for 2 weeks in an airtight container, like traditional fekkas.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Mix the egg whites, erythritol and vanilla with a fork without whipping them, then add the shredded coconut.
Let rest for 10 minutes, then shape 20 small pyramids with damp fingers on a lined baking sheet.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the tips are golden.
Once cooled, dip the bases in melted chocolate and let set on baking paper.
l11-rochers-coco.p: Ideal for using up leftover egg whites from a crème brûlée or vanilla custard.

s: Cook the butter over medium heat until it is nutty brown and smells like biscuits, then strain and let cool slightly.
Preheat the oven to 190°C and grease 12 financier molds.
Mix the almond flour, coconut flour, erythritol and salt.
Add the egg whites, lightly beaten with a fork, then the lukewarm brown butter.
Fill the molds three-quarters full and bake for 12 to 14 minutes until the edges are well golden.
Unmold while warm and let cool on a rack.
l11-financiers-amande.p: Place a raspberry in the center of each financier before baking for a fruity version.

s: Whisk the eggs with the erythritol for 3 minutes until pale.
Add the almond flour, baking powder, lemon zest and juice, then the lukewarm melted butter.
Cover and refrigerate the batter for at least 1 hour: the temperature shock makes the characteristic bump appear.
Preheat the oven to 210°C and grease a madeleine pan.
Fill the molds three-quarters full, bake for 5 minutes, then lower to 180°C and continue for 5 minutes.
Unmold immediately and let cool on a rack.
l11-madeleines-citron.p: Two madeleines per serving; they keep for 3 days in an airtight container.

s: Sponge: preheat the oven to 180°C. Whisk 2 eggs with 30 g of erythritol for 3 minutes, fold in the almond flour and spread 1 cm thick in a lined dish. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, then let cool.
Separate the other 2 eggs. Whisk the yolks with 40 g of erythritol and the vanilla, then add the mascarpone to make a smooth cream.
Whip the whites to stiff peaks and gently fold them into the mascarpone cream.
Cut the sponge into pieces, soak them in coffee and arrange a layer in the bottom of 6 small glasses.
Cover with cream, then repeat with a second layer of sponge and cream.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours and dust with cocoa just before serving.
l11-tiramisu-keto.p: For a caffeine-free version, use decaffeinated coffee. Very fresh eggs are essential. Contains raw eggs: not recommended for pregnant women, children under 5, or elderly or vulnerable people.

s: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 24 cm baking dish.
Spread the raspberries over the bottom of the dish.
Whisk the eggs with the erythritol, then add the almond flour, cream, almond milk and vanilla.
Gently pour the batter over the fruit.
Bake for 30 minutes until the clafoutis is golden and set in the center. Serve warm.
l11-clafoutis-framboises.p: Also works with blackberries or strawberries cut into quarters.

s: Blend 250 g of strawberries with the erythritol and lemon.
Pour half of the purée into a saucepan with the agar-agar, bring to a boil and boil for 2 minutes.
Off the heat, add the rest of the purée, then the fromage blanc, whisking. Let cool for 5 minutes, stirring.
Whip the cream to stiff peaks and quickly fold it into the still-soft mixture.
Pour into a charlotte mold or 6 small glasses and refrigerate for 4 hours.
Decorate with the remaining sliced strawberries when serving.
l11-bavarois-fraise.p: Unmold easily by dipping the mold in hot water for 5 seconds.

s: Whisk the coconut milk, almond milk, erythritol and vanilla.
Add the chia seeds and mix well; wait 5 minutes and stir again to prevent lumps.
Divide among 4 jars and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Top with raspberries and shredded coconut when serving.
l11-pudding-chia-coco-vanille.p: Keeps for 4 days in the refrigerator; handy for preparing the week's desserts.

l11-mendiants-chocolat.t: Chocolate mendiants with pistachios and almonds
s: Roughly chop the pistachios, almonds and hazelnuts.
Melt two-thirds of the chocolate in a bain-marie to 45°C, remove from the heat and add the chopped remainder to bring the temperature down, stirring.
Spoon 20 small chocolate discs onto a sheet of baking paper.
Immediately sprinkle with the nuts and coconut before the chocolate sets.
Let harden for 1 hour at room temperature or 20 minutes in the refrigerator.
l11-mendiants-chocolat.p: Adding chopped chocolate this way gives a glossy chocolate with a good snap. Two mendiants per serving.

s: Scoop the avocado flesh into a blender.
Add the coconut milk, cocoa, erythritol, vanilla and salt.
Blend for 2 minutes until perfectly smooth.
Pour into a container and freeze for 4 hours, stirring vigorously every hour.
Take out 10 minutes before serving and shape scoops with a warm spoon.
l11-glace-avocat-chocolat.p: Unfrozen, the mixture also makes an excellent quick chocolate mousse.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Mix the almond flour, ground hazelnuts, melted butter, 20 g of erythritol and the salt.
Press into a 22 cm tart pan, prick and bake for 12 to 15 minutes. Let cool.
Bring the cream and 30 g of erythritol to a simmer, pour over the chopped chocolate, wait 1 minute, then stir until smooth.
Pour the ganache over the cooled tart shell.
Sprinkle with crushed hazelnuts and refrigerate for 3 hours before cutting into 10 slices.
l11-tarte-chocolat-noisette.p: Take the tart out 15 minutes before serving for a soft, melting ganache.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a loaf pan.
Whisk the eggs and erythritol, then add the melted butter, vanilla and 30 ml of almond milk.
Fold in the almond flour and baking powder, then divide the batter in two.
Add the cocoa and the remaining 30 ml of almond milk to one half.
Alternate spoonfuls of the two batters in the pan and swirl with a knife.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes; cover with foil after 25 minutes. Let cool before slicing.
l11-cake-marbre.p: Perfect for the kids' snack; keeps for 4 days wrapped in plastic wrap.

s: Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease a 22 cm round pan.
Whisk the yogurt with the eggs, erythritol, oil and lemon zest.
Fold in the almond flour and baking powder until the batter is smooth.
Pour into the pan and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a knife comes out dry.
Let cool slightly before unmolding.
l11-gateau-yaourt.p: You can use the yogurt pot as a measure if you like, but weigh the almond flour, which is lighter.

s: Blend the eggs, cream cheese, almond flour and 10 g of erythritol; let rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a 20 cm nonstick skillet over medium heat with a small knob of butter.
Pour in a small ladle of batter, tilt to spread thinly and cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the edges lift, then flip for 30 seconds.
Mix the ricotta with the cinnamon and 20 g of erythritol.
Fill each crepe with ricotta cream, fold into quarters and serve warm.
l11-crepes-ricotta-cannelle.p: These crepes are delicate: use a wide spatula and keep them small. Makes about 8 crepes.

s: Preheat the oven to 170°C and line a 20 cm pan.
Grind 80 g of pistachios to a fine powder; roughly crush the rest.
Whisk the eggs and erythritol for 3 minutes, then add the melted butter and orange blossom water.
Fold in the pistachio powder, almond flour and salt.
Pour into the pan, sprinkle with crushed pistachios and bake for 22 to 25 minutes: the center stays moist.
Let cool in the pan before cutting into 8 slices.
l11-fondant-pistache.p: Pistachios are higher in carbs than almonds: stick to the serving size indicated.

s: In a saucepan, whisk the almond milk, cream, cocoa, erythritol and agar-agar while cold.
Bring to a boil, whisking, and boil for 2 minutes.
Off the heat, add the chopped chocolate and vanilla, then whisk until melted.
Divide among 4 jars, let cool, then refrigerate for 2 hours.
Whisk briefly with a spoon before serving for a creamier texture.
l11-creme-dessert-chocolat.p: Add a pinch of instant coffee for a mocha flavor.

l11-mini-cheesecakes-citron.t: Mini lemon cheesecakes in a muffin pan
s: Preheat the oven to 160°C and line a muffin pan with 12 liners.
Mix the almond flour, butter and 10 g of erythritol, and press 1 tablespoon into the bottom of each liner.
Smooth the cream cheese with 70 g of erythritol, add the eggs one at a time, then the zest, juice and vanilla.
Fill the liners almost to the top.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes: the center should still wobble slightly.
Let cool, then refrigerate for 3 hours before serving.
l11-mini-cheesecakes-citron.p: They freeze very well; thaw for 2 hours in the refrigerator.
